costs.Name: Pay Hate and Fate costs
costs.Hint: Using a skill adds its Hate cost (with the discounts of effects) and spends its Fate. Hate is only paid in a started combat; Fate always. The card shows what was paid and has an Undo button.

limits.Name: Usage limits
limits.Hint: Counts the uses of skills with a limit (1/Scene, SR/Scenario, 1/Round…) per character. A scene ends when the combat ends or with the GM tool; a scenario only with the GM tool.

actions.Name: Timing and action economy
actions.Hint: In combat, checks that a skill is used at the right time (Major, Minor, Move and Instant in your own Main Process, Setup in the Setup Process, Cleanup in the Cleanup Process) and that the Main Process action wasn't spent yet.

hatePerCombat.Name: Hate Top and Hate Under per combat
hatePerCombat.Hint: Puts [Hate Top] and [Hate Under] on the characters of every combat, so the +2 to Dodge and Hate Damage work with several combats at once, and everyone sees on the tokens who is Hate Top.

cleanup.Name: Regen and Decay in the Cleanup Process
cleanup.Hint: In the Cleanup Process of every round, Regen heals, then Decay deals damage (through Barrier). A summary is posted in the chat.

endOfProcess.Name: Dazed and Staggered end with the Main Process
endOfProcess.Hint: By the rules, these statuses end when the affected character's Main Process ends, unless it is Afflicted.

incapacitated.Name: Automatic Incapacitated
incapacitated.Hint: 0 HP (or 0 Max HP from Fatigue) makes a character Incapacitated, and an Incapacitated character drops to 0 HP. Incapacitated, Dead and Absent combatants skip their turn (straight to Post-Action).

endOfScene.Name: End of scene when the combat ends
endOfScene.Hint: When a started combat ends: Incapacitated Adventurers get back up with full HP, Incapacitated enemies die, and Bad and Combat Statuses end. Fatigue and Weakness stay.

revive.Name: Dead Adventurers revive at the end of the scene
revive.Hint: By the rules, a Dead Adventurer revives at the end of the scene with 1 HP and [Fatigue: Max HP − 1].

cards.Name: Attack and damage card fixes
cards.Hint: Damage is tied to the right attack, and the attack card gets a damage button. Apply doesn't work on a target that still has to dodge or that dodged, and asks before applying again. Private cards are shown to the owners of the targets.

fate.Name: Fate buttons
fate.Hint: Spend 1 Fate to: +1D on a skill's Check, reroll the hit, the dodge or a plain check, and remove a Bad Status (Fate button on the sheet's Statuses box).

content.Name: Fill in the compendium data
content.Hint: Skills, items and monsters taken from the system compendiums get what only existed as text: monster attack damage, skill damage and healing, statuses skills give, items' constant bonuses, start-of-scene statuses and the Fatigue food removes. Only what is missing is filled; nothing edited by hand is replaced.

chatTheme.Name: Parchment chat theme
chatTheme.Hint: Skill, attack and damage cards and the rolls on parchment, with the speaker's portrait.

Use.OnlySetup: Setup skills only in the Setup Process.
Use.OnlyCleanup: Cleanup skills only in the Cleanup Process.
Use.OnlyBriefing: Briefing skills only before the combat starts.
Use.OnlyOutOfCombat: This skill is used outside combat.

ActionSpent.major: The Major Action of this Main Process was already used.
ActionSpent.minor: The Minor Action of this Main Process was already used.
ActionSpent.move: The Move Action of this Main Process was already used.

Use.Group: Group cost ({group}): the allies pay separately
Use.UndoHint: Gives back the Hate, the Fate, the use and the action. Effects the skill applied are not removed.

Cards.PendingDodge: {name} hasn't rolled the Dodge yet: roll it on the attack card before applying.
Cards.AlreadyApplied: {name} already took this damage ({result}). Apply again?

Fate.ExtraDieHint: Roll the Check with +1D, spending 1 Fate.
Fate.UseHint: Spend 1 Fate to remove a Bad Status.
Fate.RemoveIntro: Spend 1 Fate to remove one Bad Status of {name} (Fate: {fate}).
Fate.AfflictedNote: Afflicted: Staggered, Dazed, Confused and Overconfident can only go after Afflicted.
Fate.NoBadStatus: {name} has no Bad Status to remove.

Scene.Title: End of scene
Scene.Recovered: {name} gets back up with full HP.

Tools.Name: GM tools
Tools.Label: Open
Tools.Hint: End the scene or the scenario of characters (resets the per-scene and per-scenario usage limits).
Tools.Title: Log Horizon — GM tools
Tools.Intro: Per-scene and per-scenario usage limits count per character. Ending a combat already ends the scene of those who fought; here you end scenes outside combat, and scenarios.
Tools.SceneSelected: End the scene of the selected tokens
Tools.ScenarioSelected: End the scenario of the selected tokens
Tools.ScenarioAll: End the scenario of every character
Tools.FillIntro: Fills the data of what is already in the world (items, characters, monsters and tokens): damage, statuses, bonuses and food. Homebrew monsters get their attack damage read from their text.
Tools.FillNothing: Nothing to fill: the world already has the data.
Tools.FillConfirm: This fills {documents} skills and items: {damage} with damage, {effects} with effects and {flags} with scene or food data. Only what is missing is filled. Go on?
Tools.FillDone: Data filled in: {documents} skills and items ({damage} with damage, {effects} with effects, {flags} with scene or food data).

Sheet.Label: Parchment sheet (Automação)
Sheet.RemoveBadHint: Spend 1 Fate to remove a Bad Status.
Sheet.EquipHint: drag an item onto a slot
Sheet.SpaceHint: Space used by the carried items / space of the bag.
Sheet.BioHint: Click the pencil to write the biography.
Sheet.HateBox: Hate {value}: the box fills a step per point, up to 10.
Sheet.FatigueBox: Fatigue {value}: the maximum HP drops by {value}. The box shows how much of the maximum HP Fatigue took.
